Adhyaya counts (Vana 315, Udyoga 196, Shanti 375, Anushasana 274, Ashvamedhika 118) match a southern-recension printed text of the Kumbhakonam type, not the Pune critical edition (Shanti 353, Anushasana 154, Ashvamedhika 96).

lines.deva:
किंस्विदादित्यमुन्नयति के च तस्याभितश्चराः ।
कश्चैनमस्तं नयति कस्मिंश्च प्रतितिष्ठति ॥
lines.iast:
kiṃsvidādityamunnayati ke ca tasyābhitaścarāḥ |
kaścainamastaṃ nayati kasmiṃśca pratitiṣṭhati ||
lines.en: What raises the sun? Who walk beside it? What brings it to its setting? In what does it stand firm?

lines.deva:
ब्रह्मादित्यमुन्नयति देवास्तस्याभितश्चराः ।
धर्मश्चास्तं नयति च सत्ये च प्रतितिष्ठति ॥
lines.iast:
brahmādityamunnayati devāstasyābhitaścarāḥ |
dharmaścāstaṃ nayati ca satye ca pratitiṣṭhati ||
lines.en: Brahman raises the sun. The gods walk beside it. Dharma brings it to its setting, and it stands firm in truth.

lines.deva:
केन स्विच्छ्रोत्रियो भवति केन स्विद्विन्दते महत् ।
केन स्विद्द्वितीयवान्भवति राजन्केन च बुद्धिमान् ॥
lines.iast:
kena svicchrotriyo bhavati kena svidvindate mahat |
kena sviddvitīyavānbhavati rājankena ca buddhimān ||
lines.en: How does one become learned? How does one reach what is great? How does one gain a companion, King? And how does one become wise?
lines.corpus: केन स्विच्छ्रोत्रियो भवति केन स्विद्विन्दते महत् / केन स्विद्द्वितीयवान्भवतिराजन्केन च बुद्दिमान्

lines.deva:
श्रुतेन श्रोत्रियो भवति तपसा विन्दते महत् ।
धृत्या द्वितीयवान्भवति बुद्धिमान्वृद्धसेवया ॥
lines.iast:
śrutena śrotriyo bhavati tapasā vindate mahat |
dhṛtyā dvitīyavānbhavati buddhimānvṛddhasevayā ||
lines.en: By hearing the Veda one becomes learned. By tapas one reaches what is great. By steadiness one gains a companion. By serving elders one becomes wise.
lines.corpus: श्रुतेन श्रोत्रियो भति रतपसा विन्दते महत् / धृत्या द्वितीयवान्भवति बुद्धिमान्वृद्धसेवया

lines.deva:
किंस्विद्गुरुतरं भूमेः किंस्विदुच्चतरं च खात् ।
किंस्विच्छीघ्रतरं वायोः किंस्विद्बहुतरं तृणात् ॥
lines.iast:
kiṃsvidgurutaraṃ bhūmeḥ kiṃsviduccataraṃ ca khāt |
kiṃsvicchīghrataraṃ vāyoḥ kiṃsvidbahutaraṃ tṛṇāt ||
lines.en: What is heavier than the earth? What is higher than the sky? What is faster than the wind? What is more numerous than grass?
lines.corpus: किंस्विद्गुरुतरं भूमेः किंस्विदुच्चतरं च स्वात् / किंस्विच्छीघ्रतरं वायोः किंस्विद्बहुतरं तृणात्

lines.deva:
माता गुरुतरा भूमेः खात्पितोच्चतरस्तथा ।
मनः शीघ्रतरं वाताच्चिन्ता बहुतरी तृणात् ॥
lines.iast:
mātā gurutarā bhūmeḥ khātpitoccatarastathā |
manaḥ śīghrataraṃ vātāccintā bahutarī tṛṇāt ||
lines.en: A mother is heavier than the earth. A father is higher than the sky. The mind is faster than the wind. Worries outnumber the grass.
lines.hi: माँ धरती से भारी है, पिता आकाश से ऊँचे। मन हवा से तेज़ है, और चिंताएँ घास से भी ज़्यादा।

lines.deva:
किंस्वित्सुप्तं न निमिषति किंस्विज्जातं न चेङ्गते ।
कस्यस्विद्धृदयं नास्ति किंस्विद्वेगेन वर्धते ॥
lines.iast:
kiṃsvitsuptaṃ na nimiṣati kiṃsvijjātaṃ na ceṅgate |
kasyasviddhṛdayaṃ nāsti kiṃsvidvegena vardhate ||
lines.en: What does not close its eyes in sleep? What does not move once it is born? What has no heart? What swells by its own rush?
lines.corpus: किंस्वित्सुप्तं न निमिषति किंस्विज्जातं न चेङ्गते / कस्यस्विद्धृदयं नास्तिकास्विद्वेगेन वर्धते

lines.deva:
मत्स्यः सुप्तो न निमिषत्यण्डं जातं न चेङ्गते ।
अश्मनो हृदयं नास्ति नदी वेगेन वर्धते ॥
lines.iast:
matsyaḥ supto na nimiṣatyaṇḍaṃ jātaṃ na ceṅgate |
aśmano hṛdayaṃ nāsti nadī vegena vardhate ||
lines.en: A fish sleeps with its eyes open. An egg, once born, does not move. A stone has no heart. A river swells by its own rush.

lines.deva:
किंस्वित्प्रवसतो मित्रं किंस्विन्मित्रं गृहे सतः ।
आतुरस्य च किं मित्रं किंस्विन्मित्रं मरिष्यतः ॥
lines.iast:
kiṃsvitpravasato mitraṃ kiṃsvinmitraṃ gṛhe sataḥ |
āturasya ca kiṃ mitraṃ kiṃsvinmitraṃ mariṣyataḥ ||
lines.en: Who is the friend of one far from home? Of one at home? Of one who is ill? Of one about to die?
lines.corpus: किंस्वित्प्रवसतो मित्रं किंस्विन्मित्रं गृहे सतः / आतुरस् च किं मित्रं किंस्विन्मित्रं मरिष्यतः

lines.deva:
विद्या प्रवसतो मित्रं भार्या मित्रं गृहे सतः ।
आतुरस्य भिषङ्मित्रं दानं मित्रं मरिष्यतः ॥
lines.iast:
vidyā pravasato mitraṃ bhāryā mitraṃ gṛhe sataḥ |
āturasya bhiṣaṅmitraṃ dānaṃ mitraṃ mariṣyataḥ ||
lines.en: Learning is the friend of one far from home. A wife is the friend at home. The doctor is the friend of the sick. What you have given away is the friend of the dying.
lines.corpus: विद्या प्रवसतो मित्रं भार्या मित्रं गृहे सतः / आतुरस्य भिषङ्भित्रं दानं मित्रं मरिष्यतः

lines.deva:
धन्यानामुत्तमं किंस्विद्धनानां स्यात्किमुत्तमम् ।
लाभानामुत्तमं किं स्यात्सुखानां स्यात्किमुत्तमम् ॥
lines.iast:
dhanyānāmuttamaṃ kiṃsviddhanānāṃ syātkimuttamam |
lābhānāmuttamaṃ kiṃ syātsukhānāṃ syātkimuttamam ||
lines.en: What is the best thing to be praised for? The best of wealth? The best of gains? The best of joys?
lines.corpus: धन्यानामुत्तमं किंस्विद्धनानां स्यात्किमुत्तमम् / लाभानामुत्तमं किंस्यात्सुखानां स्यात्किमुत्तमं

lines.deva:
धन्यानामुत्तमं दाक्ष्यं धनानामुत्तमं श्रुतम् ।
लाभानां श्रेय आरोग्यं सुखानां तुष्टिरुत्तमा ॥
lines.iast:
dhanyānāmuttamaṃ dākṣyaṃ dhanānāmuttamaṃ śrutam |
lābhānāṃ śreya ārogyaṃ sukhānāṃ tuṣṭiruttamā ||
lines.en: Skill is the best thing to be praised for. Learning is the best wealth. Health is the best gain. Contentment is the best joy.

lines.deva:
किंनु हित्वा प्रियो भवति किंनु हित्वा न शोचति ।
किंनु हित्वाऽर्थवान्भवति किंनु हित्वा सुखी भवेत् ॥
lines.iast:
kiṃnu hitvā priyo bhavati kiṃnu hitvā na śocati |
kiṃnu hitvā'rthavānbhavati kiṃnu hitvā sukhī bhavet ||
lines.en: Giving up what makes a person loved? Giving up what ends grief? Giving up what makes one rich? Giving up what makes one happy?

lines.deva:
मानं हित्वा प्रियो भवति क्रोधं हित्वा न शोचति ।
कामं हित्वाऽर्थवान्भवति लोभं हित्वा सुखी भवेत् ॥
lines.iast:
mānaṃ hitvā priyo bhavati krodhaṃ hitvā na śocati |
kāmaṃ hitvā'rthavānbhavati lobhaṃ hitvā sukhī bhavet ||
lines.en: Give up pride and you are loved. Give up anger and you stop grieving. Give up craving and you are rich. Give up greed and you are happy.
lines.corpus: मानं हित्वाप्रियो भवति क्रोधं हित्वा न शोचति / कामं हित्वाऽर्थवान्भवति लोमं हित्वा सुखी भवेत्

lines.deva:
तपः किंलक्षणं प्रोक्तं को दमश्च प्रकीर्तितः ।
क्षमा च का परा प्रोक्ता का च ह्रीः परिकीर्तिता ॥
lines.iast:
tapaḥ kiṃlakṣaṇaṃ proktaṃ ko damaśca prakīrtitaḥ |
kṣamā ca kā parā proktā kā ca hrīḥ parikīrtitā ||
lines.en: What is the mark of tapas? What is self-control? What is the highest forbearance? What is called shame?

lines.deva:
तपः स्वधर्मवर्तित्वं मनसो दमनं दमः ।
क्षमा द्वन्द्वसहिष्णुत्वं ह्रीरकार्यनिवर्तनम् ॥
lines.iast:
tapaḥ svadharmavartitvaṃ manaso damanaṃ damaḥ |
kṣamā dvandvasahiṣṇutvaṃ hrīrakāryanivartanam ||
lines.en: Tapas is living by your own dharma. Self-control is mastering the mind. Forbearance is bearing the pairs, like heat and cold, praise and blame. Shame is turning back from a wrong act.
lines.corpus: तपः स्वधर्मवर्तित्वं मनसो दमनं दमः / क्षमा द्वन्द्वसहिष्णुत्वंहीरकार्यनिवर्तनम्

lines.deva:
कः शत्रुर्दुर्जयः पुंसां कश्च व्याधिरनन्तकः ।
कीदृशश्च स्मृतः साधुरसाधुः कीदृशः स्मृतः ॥
lines.iast:
kaḥ śatrurdurjayaḥ puṃsāṃ kaśca vyādhiranantakaḥ |
kīdṛśaśca smṛtaḥ sādhurasādhuḥ kīdṛśaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
lines.en: Which enemy is hardest to defeat? Which illness has no end? Who is called good, and who is called bad?

lines.deva:
क्रोधः सुदुर्जयः शत्रुर्लोभो व्याधिरनन्तकः ।
सर्वभूतहितः साधुरसाधुर्निर्दयः स्मृतः ॥
lines.iast:
krodhaḥ sudurjayaḥ śatrurlobho vyādhiranantakaḥ |
sarvabhūtahitaḥ sādhurasādhurnirdayaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
lines.en: Anger is the enemy hardest to defeat. Greed is the illness with no end. The good person wants the good of every being. The bad person has no mercy.

lines.deva:
किं स्थैर्यमृषिभिः प्रोक्तं किं च धैर्यमुदाहृतम् ।
स्नानं च किं परं प्रोक्तं दानं च किमिहोच्यते ॥
lines.iast:
kiṃ sthairyamṛṣibhiḥ proktaṃ kiṃ ca dhairyamudāhṛtam |
snānaṃ ca kiṃ paraṃ proktaṃ dānaṃ ca kimihocyate ||
lines.en: What do the sages call steadiness? What is courage? What is the true bath? What is giving?

lines.deva:
स्वधर्मे स्थिरता स्थैर्यं धैर्यमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः ।
स्नानं मनोमलत्यागो दानं वै भूतरक्षणम् ॥
lines.iast:
svadharme sthiratā sthairyaṃ dhairyamindriyanigrahaḥ |
snānaṃ manomalatyāgo dānaṃ vai bhūtarakṣaṇam ||
lines.en: Steadiness is standing firm in your own dharma. Courage is mastering the senses. The true bath is washing the mind clean. Giving is protecting living beings.

lines.deva:
राजन्कुलेन वृत्तेन स्वाध्यायेन श्रुतेन वा ।
ब्राह्मण्यं केन भवति प्रब्रूह्येतत्सुनिश्चितम् ॥
lines.iast:
rājankulena vṛttena svādhyāyena śrutena vā |
brāhmaṇyaṃ kena bhavati prabrūhyetatsuniścitam ||
lines.en: King, what makes a brahmana: birth, conduct, recitation or learning? Tell me plainly.

lines.deva:
शृणु यक्ष कुलं तात न स्वाध्यायो न च श्रुतम् ।
कारणं हि द्विजत्वे च वृत्तमेव न संशयः ॥
lines.iast:
śṛṇu yakṣa kulaṃ tāta na svādhyāyo na ca śrutam |
kāraṇaṃ hi dvijatve ca vṛttameva na saṃśayaḥ ||
lines.en: Listen, Yaksha, my friend. Conduct alone makes one twice-born, beyond doubt. Birth, recitation and learning do not.

lines.deva:
को मोदते किमाश्चर्यं कः पन्थाः का च वार्तिका ।
वद मे चतुरः प्रश्नान्मृता जीवन्तु बान्धवाः ॥
lines.iast:
ko modate kimāścaryaṃ kaḥ panthāḥ kā ca vārtikā |
vada me caturaḥ praśnānmṛtā jīvantu bāndhavāḥ ||
lines.en: Who is happy? What is the wonder? What is the path? What is the news? Answer these four and your dead brothers may live.

lines.deva:
पञ्चमेऽहनि षष्ठे वा शाकं पचति स्वे गृहे ।
अनृणी चाप्रवासी च स वारिचर मोदते ॥
lines.iast:
pañcame'hani ṣaṣṭhe vā śākaṃ pacati sve gṛhe |
anṛṇī cāpravāsī ca sa vāricara modate ||
lines.en: One who cooks greens in his own home on the fifth day or the sixth, owing nothing and living at home: he is happy, creature of the water.
lines.corpus: पञ्चमेऽहनि षष्ठे वा शाकं पचति स्वे गृहे / अनृणी रचाप्रवासी चस वारिचर मोदते

lines.deva:
अहन्यहनि भूतानि गच्छन्तीह यमालयम् ।
शेषाः स्थावरमिच्छन्ति किमाश्चर्यमतः परम् ॥
lines.iast:
ahanyahani bhūtāni gacchantīha yamālayam |
śeṣāḥ sthāvaramicchanti kimāścaryamataḥ param ||
lines.en: Day after day, living beings go to the house of death. Those left behind want to stay forever. What could be a greater wonder?
lines.hi: हर दिन प्राणी यमलोक जाते हैं, फिर भी जो बचे हैं वे हमेशा रहना चाहते हैं। इससे बड़ा आश्चर्य क्या?

lines.deva:
तर्कोऽप्रतिष्ठः श्रुतयो विभिन्ना
नैको मुनिर्यस्य मतं प्रमाणम् ।
धर्मस्य तत्त्वं निहितं गुहायां
महाजनो येन गतः स पन्थाः ॥
lines.iast:
tarko'pratiṣṭhaḥ śrutayo vibhinnā
naiko muniryasya mataṃ pramāṇam |
dharmasya tattvaṃ nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ
mahājano yena gataḥ sa panthāḥ ||
lines.en: Reasoning has no firm footing. The scriptures differ. No single sage has the final word. The truth of dharma lies hidden in a cave. The path is the one the great have walked.
lines.hi: तर्क की ज़मीन पक्की नहीं, शास्त्र अलग-अलग कहते हैं, किसी एक मुनि की बात आख़िरी नहीं। धर्म का सच गुफा में छिपा है। रास्ता वही है जिस पर महापुरुष चले।
lines.note: Nilakantha reads mahājana as the great and good, those whose conduct is the standard; some read it as "the many". We follow Nilakantha.
lines.corpus: तर्कोऽप्रतिष्ठः श्रुतयो विभिन्ना / नैको मुनिर्यस्य मतं प्रमाणम् / धर्मस्य तत्त्वं निहितं गुहायां / महाजनो येन गतःस पन्था

lines.deva:
पृथ्वी विभाण्डं गगनं पिधानं
सूर्याग्निना रात्रिदिवेन्धनेन ।
मासर्तुदर्वीपरिघट्टनेन
भूतानि कालः पचतीति वार्ता ॥
lines.iast:
pṛthvī vibhāṇḍaṃ gaganaṃ pidhānaṃ
sūryāgninā rātridivendhanena |
māsartudarvīparighaṭṭanena
bhūtāni kālaḥ pacatīti vārtā ||
lines.en: The earth is the pot and the sky its lid. With the sun for fire and nights and days for fuel, stirring with the ladle of months and seasons, Time cooks all beings. That is the news.
lines.note: Our southern text opens with "pṛthvī vibhāṇḍaṃ gaganaṃ pidhānaṃ"; the vulgate reads "asmin mahāmohamaye kaṭāhe". We translate our reading.
lines.corpus: पृथ्वी विभाण्डं गगनं पिघानं / सूर्याग्निना रात्रिदिवेन्धनेन / मासर्तुदर्वीपरिघट्टनेन / भूतानि कालः पचतीति वार्ता

lines.deva:
प्रियस्ते भीमसेनोऽयमर्जुनो वः परायणम् ।
त्वं कस्मान्नकुलं राजन्सापत्नं जीवमिच्छसि ॥
lines.iast:
priyaste bhīmaseno'yamarjuno vaḥ parāyaṇam |
tvaṃ kasmānnakulaṃ rājansāpatnaṃ jīvamicchasi ||
lines.en: Bhima is dear to you, and Arjuna is the one you all lean on. Why, King, do you want Nakula, your stepmother's son, to live?

lines.deva:
धर्म एव हतो हन्ति धर्मो रक्षति रक्षितः ।
तस्माद्धर्मं न त्यजामि मा नो धर्मो हतोऽवधीत् ॥
lines.iast:
dharma eva hato hanti dharmo rakṣati rakṣitaḥ |
tasmāddharmaṃ na tyajāmi mā no dharmo hato'vadhīt ||
lines.en: Dharma destroyed destroys. Dharma protected protects. So I will not abandon dharma, or dharma, destroyed, would destroy us.
lines.hi: धर्म को नष्ट करो तो वह नष्ट करता है, धर्म की रक्षा करो तो वह रक्षा करता है। इसलिए मैं धर्म नहीं छोड़ता।
lines.corpus: धर्म एव हतो हन्ति ध्रमो रक्षति रक्षितः / तस्माद्धऱ्मं न त्यजामि मा नो धर्मो हतोऽवधीत्

lines.deva:
आनृशंस्यं परो धर्मः परमार्थाच्च मे मतम् ।
आनृशंस्यं चिकीर्षामि नकुलो यक्ष जीवतु ॥
lines.iast:
ānṛśaṃsyaṃ paro dharmaḥ paramārthācca me matam |
ānṛśaṃsyaṃ cikīrṣāmi nakulo yakṣa jīvatu ||
lines.en: Not being cruel is the highest dharma, higher to my mind than the highest gain. I want to act without cruelty. Let Nakula live, Yaksha.

lines.deva:
यथा कुन्ती तथा माद्री विशेषो नास्ति मे तयोः ।
मातृभ्यां सममिच्छामि नकुलो यक्ष जीवतु ॥
lines.iast:
yathā kuntī tathā mādrī viśeṣo nāsti me tayoḥ |
mātṛbhyāṃ samamicchāmi nakulo yakṣa jīvatu ||
lines.en: As Kunti is, so is Madri. I make no difference between them. I want the same for both my mothers. Let Nakula live, Yaksha.

lines.deva:
अहं ते जनकस्तात धर्मो मृदुपराक्रम ।
त्वां दिदृक्षुरनुप्राप्तो विद्धि मां भरतर्षभ ॥
lines.iast:
ahaṃ te janakastāta dharmo mṛduparākrama |
tvāṃ didṛkṣuranuprāpto viddhi māṃ bharatarṣabha ||
lines.en: I am your father, child: Dharma. You are gentle in your strength. Know that I came here wanting to see you, best of the Bharatas.
lines.corpus: अहंते जनकस्तात धर्मो मृदुपराक्रम / त्वां रदिदृक्षुरनुप्राप्तो विद्धि मां भरतर्षभ

lines.deva:
तृतीयं गृह्यतां पुत्र वरमप्रतिमं महत् ।
त्वं हि मत्प्रभवो राजन्विदुरश्च ममांशजः ॥
lines.iast:
tṛtīyaṃ gṛhyatāṃ putra varamapratimaṃ mahat |
tvaṃ hi matprabhavo rājanviduraśca mamāṃśajaḥ ||
lines.en: Take a third boon, son, great and without equal. You were born of me, King, and Vidura too is born of a part of me.

lines.deva:
जयेयं लोभमोहौ च क्रोधं चाहं सदा विभो ।
दाने तपसि सत्ये च मनो मे सततं भवेत् ॥
lines.iast:
jayeyaṃ lobhamohau ca krodhaṃ cāhaṃ sadā vibho |
dāne tapasi satye ca mano me satataṃ bhavet ||
lines.en: Let me always overcome greed, delusion and anger, Lord. Let my mind stay always on giving, tapas and truth.
lines.corpus: जयेयं लोभमोहौ च क्रोधं चाहं सदा विभो / दाने तपसि सत्ये च मनो मे सततं वेत्

lines.deva:
नाहं धर्मफलाकाङ्क्षी राजपुत्रि चराम्युत ।
ददामि देयमित्येव यजे यष्टव्यमित्युत ॥
lines.iast:
nāhaṃ dharmaphalākāṅkṣī rājaputri carāmyuta |
dadāmi deyamityeva yaje yaṣṭavyamityuta ||
lines.en: I do not practise dharma hungry for its fruit, princess. I give because it should be given. I worship because worship should be offered.
lines.hi: राजकुमारी, मैं धर्म का फल पाने के लिए धर्म नहीं करता। देना चाहिए, इसलिए देता हूँ; पूजा करनी चाहिए, इसलिए करता हूँ।
lines.corpus: नाहं धर्मफलाकाङ्क्षी राजपुत्रि चराम्भुत / ददामि देयमित्येव यजे यष्टव्यमित्युत

lines.deva:
धर्मं चरामि सुश्रोणि न धर्मफलकारणात् ।
आगमाननतिक्रम्य सतां वृत्तमवेक्ष्य च ॥
lines.iast:
dharmaṃ carāmi suśroṇi na dharmaphalakāraṇāt |
āgamānanatikramya satāṃ vṛttamavekṣya ca ||
lines.en: I follow dharma for its own sake, without an eye on its reward, keeping to the scriptures and watching how good people live.

lines.deva:
कर्म खल्विह कर्तव्यं जातेनामित्रकर्शन ।
अकर्माणो हि जीवन्ति स्थावरा नेतरे जनाः ॥
lines.iast:
karma khalviha kartavyaṃ jātenāmitrakarśana |
akarmāṇo hi jīvanti sthāvarā netare janāḥ ||
lines.en: Whoever is born here has to act, tamer of enemies. Only things that cannot move live without action. No one else does.
lines.hi: जो जन्मा है, उसे कर्म करना ही है। बिना कर्म के तो बस जड़ चीज़ें जीती हैं, और कोई नहीं।

lines.deva:
न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन ।
न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस्य भूतिर्भवति शोभना ॥
lines.iast:
na tvevātmā'vamantavyaḥ puruṣeṇa kadācana |
na hyātmaparibhūtasya bhūtirbhavati śobhanā ||
lines.en: No one should ever think little of themselves. One who holds themselves in contempt does not flourish.
lines.hi: इंसान को खुद को कभी छोटा नहीं समझना चाहिए। जो अपना ही अपमान करता है, उसका भला नहीं होता।
lines.corpus: न त्वेवात्माऽवमन्तव्यः पुरुषेण कदाचन / न ह्यात्मपरिभूतस् भूतिर्भवति शोभना

lines.deva:
स मां राजन्कर्मवतीमागतामाह सान्त्वयन् ।
शुश्रूषमाणामासीनां पितुरङ्के युधिष्ठिर ॥
lines.iast:
sa māṃ rājankarmavatīmāgatāmāha sāntvayan |
śuśrūṣamāṇāmāsīnāṃ pituraṅke yudhiṣṭhira ||
lines.en: He taught it to me too, King, gently, when I came in on some errand and sat listening on my father's lap, Yudhishthira.
lines.context: Draupadi explains where she learned Brihaspati's statecraft: from a learned brahmana her father kept at court, who taught it to her brothers (MBh 3.32.60 to 61).

lines.deva:
सोऽस्य दोषो न मन्तव्यः क्षमा हि परमं बलम् ।
क्षमा गुणो ह्यशक्तानां शक्तानां भूषणं क्षमा ॥
lines.iast:
so'sya doṣo na mantavyaḥ kṣamā hi paramaṃ balam |
kṣamā guṇo hyaśaktānāṃ śaktānāṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ kṣamā ||
lines.en: Do not count that as a fault, for forbearance is the greatest strength. In the weak, forbearance is a virtue. In the strong, it is an ornament.

lines.deva:
त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः ।
कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥
lines.iast:
trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ |
kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet ||
lines.en: Three gates lead to hell and ruin the self: desire, anger and greed. So give up these three.
lines.hi: नरक के तीन दरवाज़े हैं जो इंसान को नष्ट करते हैं: काम, क्रोध और लोभ। इसलिए इन तीनों को छोड़ दो।
lines.note: Word for word the same verse as Bhagavad Gita 16.21.
lines.corpus: त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः / कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्रयं त्यजेत्

lines.deva:
षड्दोषाः पुरुषेणेह हातव्या भूतिमिच्छता ।
निद्रा तन्द्री भयं क्रोध आलस्यं दीर्घसूत्रता ॥
lines.iast:
ṣaḍdoṣāḥ puruṣeṇeha hātavyā bhūtimicchatā |
nidrā tandrī bhayaṃ krodha ālasyaṃ dīrghasūtratā ||
lines.en: Anyone who wants to do well in life should drop six faults: too much sleep, drowsiness, fear, anger, idleness and putting things off.
lines.hi: जो आगे बढ़ना चाहे, वह छह दोष छोड़े: ज़्यादा नींद, ऊँघ, डर, गुस्सा, आलस और टालमटोल।

lines.deva:
प्रदायैषामुचितं तात राज्यं
सुखी पुत्रैः सहितो मोदमानः ।
न देवानां नापि च मानुषाणां
भविष्यसि त्वं गर्हणीयो नरेन्द्र ॥
lines.iast:
pradāyaiṣāmucitaṃ tāta rājyaṃ
sukhī putraiḥ sahito modamānaḥ |
na devānāṃ nāpi ca mānuṣāṇāṃ
bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ garhaṇīyo narendra ||
lines.en: Give them their rightful kingdom, dear one, and live happily among your sons. Then neither gods nor people will find fault with you, King.

lines.deva:
आत्मनात्मानमन्विच्छेन्मनोबुद्धीन्द्रियैर्यतैः ।
आत्मा ह्येवात्मनो बन्धुरात्मैव रिपुरात्मनः ॥
lines.iast:
ātmanātmānamanvicchenmanobuddhīndriyairyataiḥ |
ātmā hyevātmano bandhurātmaiva ripurātmanaḥ ||
lines.en: Seek the self through the self, with mind, intellect and senses held steady. The self alone is the self's friend, and the self alone its enemy.
lines.hi: मन, बुद्धि और इंद्रियों को साधकर अपने आप को खोजो। आत्मा ही आत्मा का मित्र है, और वही उसका शत्रु।
lines.note: The second half matches Bhagavad Gita 6.5 (ātmaiva hy ātmano bandhur ātmaiva ripur ātmanaḥ).

lines.deva:
क्षुद्राक्षेणेव जालेन झषावपिहितावुरू ।
कामश्च राजन्क्रोधश्च तौ प्रज्ञानं विलुम्पतः ॥
lines.iast:
kṣudrākṣeṇeva jālena jhaṣāvapihitāvurū |
kāmaśca rājankrodhaśca tau prajñānaṃ vilumpataḥ ||
lines.en: As two big fish tear through a fine net, King, desire and anger tear through a person's judgement.
lines.note: Corpus reads झपावपिहितावुरू; emended to झषौ (two fish). We follow the reading where the fish break the net, as Ganguli does.
lines.corpus: क्षुद्राक्षेणेव जालेन झपावपिहितावुरू / कामश्च राजन्क्रोधश्च तौ प्रज्ञानं विलुम्पतः

lines.deva:
रोहते सायकैर्विद्धं वनं परशुना हतम् ।
वाचा दुरुक्तं बीभत्सं न संरोहति वाक्क्षतम् ॥
lines.iast:
rohate sāyakairviddhaṃ vanaṃ paraśunā hatam |
vācā duruktaṃ bībhatsaṃ na saṃrohati vākkṣatam ||
lines.en: Flesh pierced by arrows heals, and a forest cut down by the axe grows back. A wound from cruel words does not heal.

lines.deva:
न सा सभा यत्र न सन्ति वृद्धा
न ते वृद्धा ये न वदन्ति धर्मम् ।
नासौ धर्मो यत्र न सत्यमस्ति
न तत्सत्यं यच्छलेनानुविद्धम् ॥
lines.iast:
na sā sabhā yatra na santi vṛddhā
na te vṛddhā ye na vadanti dharmam |
nāsau dharmo yatra na satyamasti
na tatsatyaṃ yacchalenānuviddham ||
lines.en: A hall without elders is no assembly. Elders who do not speak up for dharma are no elders. Dharma without truth is no dharma. Truth laced with deceit is no truth.

lines.deva:
आक्रुश्यमानो नाक्रोशेन्मन्युरेव तितिक्षतः ।
आक्रोष्टारं निर्दहति सुकृतं चास्य विन्दति ॥
lines.iast:
ākruśyamāno nākrośenmanyureva titikṣataḥ |
ākroṣṭāraṃ nirdahati sukṛtaṃ cāsya vindati ||

speaker.en: The swan's teaching, as Vidura tells it
speaker.hi: हंस का उपदेश, विदुर के मुख से

lines.en: When someone abuses you, do not abuse them back. The hurt of one who bears it burns the abuser, and the abuser's merit passes to the one who endured.
lines.note: Nilakantha: the suppressed hurt (manyu) of the forbearing burns the abuser; the forbearer gains the abuser's merit. The same verse appears in the Shanti Parva (our mbh.12.305.16).

lines.deva:
अव्याहृतं व्याहृताच्छ्रेय आहुः
सत्यं वदेद्व्याहृतं तद्द्वितीयम् ।
प्रियं वदेद्व्याहृतं तत्तृतीयं
धर्म्यं वदेद्व्याहृतं तच्चतुर्थम् ॥
lines.iast:
avyāhṛtaṃ vyāhṛtācchreya āhuḥ
satyaṃ vadedvyāhṛtaṃ taddvitīyam |
priyaṃ vadedvyāhṛtaṃ tattṛtīyaṃ
dharmyaṃ vadedvyāhṛtaṃ taccaturtham ||

speaker.en: The swan's teaching, as Vidura tells it
speaker.hi: हंस का उपदेश, विदुर के मुख से

lines.en: Silence is better than speech, they say. If you speak, speak the truth: that is the second step. Say it kindly: the third. Say what is right: the fourth.

lines.deva:
यादृशैः सन्निविशते यादृशांश्चोपसेवते ।
यादृगिच्छेच्च भवितुं तादृग्भवति पूरुषः ॥
lines.iast:
yādṛśaiḥ sanniviśate yādṛśāṃścopasevate |
yādṛgicchecca bhavituṃ tādṛgbhavati pūruṣaḥ ||

speaker.en: The swan's teaching, as Vidura tells it
speaker.hi: हंस का उपदेश, विदुर के मुख से

lines.en: A person becomes like the people they sit with, like the people they serve, and like what they wish to become.

lines.deva:
अव्याधिजं कटुकं शीर्षरोगि
पापानुबन्धं परुषं तीक्ष्णमुष्णम् ।
सतां पेयं यन्न पिबन्त्यसन्तो
मन्युं महाराज पिब प्रशाम्य ॥
lines.iast:
avyādhijaṃ kaṭukaṃ śīrṣarogi
pāpānubandhaṃ paruṣaṃ tīkṣṇamuṣṇam |
satāṃ peyaṃ yanna pibantyasanto
manyuṃ mahārāja piba praśāmya ||
lines.en: It is bitter. It gives a headache with no illness behind it. It brings wrong in its wake, harsh, sharp and hot. The good drink it down and the bad cannot. Drink down your anger, great King, and be at peace.

lines.deva:
सुलभाः पुरुषा राजन्सततं प्रियवादिनः ।
अप्रियस्य तु पथ्यस्य वक्ता श्रोता च दुर्लभः ॥
lines.iast:
sulabhāḥ puruṣā rājansatataṃ priyavādinaḥ |
apriyasya tu pathyasya vaktā śrotā ca durlabhaḥ ||
lines.en: People who always say pleasant things are easy to find, King. Rare is the one who says what is unwelcome but good for you, and rare the one who listens.
lines.hi: राजन्, हमेशा मीठा बोलने वाले आसानी से मिल जाते हैं। कड़वी पर हित की बात कहने वाला और उसे सुनने वाला, दोनों दुर्लभ हैं।

lines.deva:
त्यजेत्कुलार्थे पुरुषं ग्रामस्यार्थे कुलं त्यजेत् ।
ग्रामं जनपदस्यार्थे आत्मार्थे पृथिवीं त्यजेत् ॥
lines.iast:
tyajetkulārthe puruṣaṃ grāmasyārthe kulaṃ tyajet |
grāmaṃ janapadasyārthe ātmārthe pṛthivīṃ tyajet ||
lines.en: Give up one person to save a family, a family to save a village, a village to save a country, and the whole earth to save your self.
lines.context: Vidura is pressing Dhritarashtra to give up Duryodhana for the sake of the family.

lines.deva:
सन्नियच्छति यो वेगमुत्थितं क्रोधहर्षयोः ।
स श्रियो भाजनं राजन्यश्चापत्सु न मुह्यति ॥
lines.iast:
sanniyacchati yo vegamutthitaṃ krodhaharṣayoḥ |
sa śriyo bhājanaṃ rājanyaścāpatsu na muhyati ||
lines.en: One who reins in the surge of anger or elation as it rises, and keeps a clear head in trouble, is the one good fortune comes to, King.

lines.deva:
उक्तं मया जातमात्रेऽपि राजन्
दुर्योधनं त्यज पुत्रं त्वमेकम् ।
तस्य त्यागात्पुत्रशतस्य वृद्धि-
रस्यात्यागात्पुत्रशतस्य नाशः ॥
lines.iast:
uktaṃ mayā jātamātre'pi rājan
duryodhanaṃ tyaja putraṃ tvamekam |
tasya tyāgātputraśatasya vṛddhi-
rasyātyāgātputraśatasya nāśaḥ ||
lines.en: I told you the day he was born, King: give up this one son, Duryodhana. Give him up and your hundred sons will thrive. Keep him and the hundred will perish.

lines.deva:
सर्वं त्वमायतीयुक्तं भाषसे प्राज्ञसंमतम् ।
न चोत्सहे सुतं त्यक्तुं यतो धर्मस्ततो जयः ॥
lines.iast:
sarvaṃ tvamāyatīyuktaṃ bhāṣase prājñasaṃmatam |
na cotsahe sutaṃ tyaktuṃ yato dharmastato jayaḥ ||
lines.en: Everything you say looks ahead, and the wise would agree with it. Still, I cannot bring myself to give up my son. Where dharma is, there is victory.
lines.hi: तुम्हारी हर बात दूर की सोचती है और समझदार भी यही कहेंगे। फिर भी मैं अपने बेटे को नहीं छोड़ पाता। जहाँ धर्म है, वहीं जीत है।

lines.deva:
अकीर्तिं विनयो हन्ति हन्त्यनर्थं पराक्रमः ।
हन्ति नित्यं क्षमा क्रोधमाचारो हन्त्यलक्षणम् ॥
lines.iast:
akīrtiṃ vinayo hanti hantyanarthaṃ parākramaḥ |
hanti nityaṃ kṣamā krodhamācāro hantyalakṣaṇam ||
lines.en: Humility undoes disgrace. Effort undoes misfortune. Forbearance always undoes anger. Good conduct undoes bad omens.
lines.corpus: अकीर्ति विनयो हन्ति हन्त्यनर्थं पराक्रमः / हन्ति नित्यं क्षमा क्रोधमाचारो हन्त्यलक्षणम्

lines.deva:
न तत्परस्य सन्दध्यात्प्रतिकूलं यदात्मनः ।
सङ्ग्रहेणैव धर्मः स्यात्कामादन्यः प्रवर्तते ॥
lines.iast:
na tatparasya sandadhyātpratikūlaṃ yadātmanaḥ |
saṅgraheṇaiva dharmaḥ syātkāmādanyaḥ pravartate ||
lines.en: Do not do to another what you would not want done to you. That, in short, is dharma. Anything else comes from desire.
lines.note: The same rule appears in the Anushasana Parva (our mbh.13.175.8), there from Brihaspati.

lines.deva:
अक्रोधेन जयेत्क्रोधमसाधुं साधुना जयेत् ।
जयेत्कदर्यं दानेन जयेत्सत्येन चानृतम् ॥
lines.iast:
akrodhena jayetkrodhamasādhuṃ sādhunā jayet |
jayetkadaryaṃ dānena jayetsatyena cānṛtam ||
lines.en: Win over anger with calm, the wicked with goodness, the miser with giving, and the liar with truth.
lines.hi: क्रोध को शांति से जीतो, दुष्ट को भलाई से, कंजूस को दान से और झूठे को सच से।
lines.corpus: अक्रोधेन जयेत्क्रोधमसाधुं नाधुना जयेत् / जयेत्कदर्यं दानेन जयेन्मत्येन चानृतम्

lines.deva:
इदं च त्वां सर्वपरं ब्रवीमि
पुण्यं पदं तात महाविशिष्टम् ।
न जातु कामान्न भयान्न लोभा-
द्धर्मं जह्याज्जीवितस्यापि हेतोः ॥
lines.iast:
idaṃ ca tvāṃ sarvaparaṃ bravīmi
puṇyaṃ padaṃ tāta mahāviśiṣṭam |
na jātu kāmānna bhayānna lobhā-
ddharmaṃ jahyājjīvitasyāpi hetoḥ ||
lines.en: And above all I tell you this, dear one, a holy step and the highest: never give up dharma for desire, for fear or for greed, not even to save your life.
lines.hi: सबसे बढ़कर यह कहता हूँ: कामना, डर या लालच के लिए धर्म कभी मत छोड़ो, जान बचाने के लिए भी नहीं।
lines.corpus: इदं च त्वां सर्वपरं ब्रवीमि / पुण्यं पदं तात महाविशिष्टम् / न जातु कामान्न भयान्न लोभा- / द्धर्मं जह्याज्जीविस्यापि हेतोः

lines.deva:
नित्यो धर्मः सुखदुःखे त्वनित्ये
जीवो नित्यो धातुरस्य त्वनित्यः ।
त्यक्त्वाऽनित्यं प्रतितिष्ठस्व नित्ये
संतुष्य सन्तोषपरा हि सन्तः ॥
lines.iast:
nityo dharmaḥ sukhaduḥkhe tvanitye
jīvo nityo dhāturasya tvanityaḥ |
tyaktvā'nityaṃ pratitiṣṭhasva nitye
saṃtuṣya santoṣaparā hi santaḥ ||
lines.en: Dharma lasts. Pleasure and pain pass. The living self lasts; its body passes. Let go of what passes and stand on what lasts. Be content: the good hold contentment highest.

lines.deva:
कामक्रोधग्राहवतीं पञ्चेन्द्रियजलां नदीम् ।
नावं धृतिमयीं कृत्वा जन्मदुर्गाणि संतर ॥
lines.iast:
kāmakrodhagrāhavatīṃ pañcendriyajalāṃ nadīm |
nāvaṃ dhṛtimayīṃ kṛtvā janmadurgāṇi saṃtara ||
lines.en: There is a river whose water is the five senses and whose crocodiles are desire and anger. Make a boat of steadiness and cross the hard passages of birth.

lines.deva:
साऽहं केशग्रहं प्राप्ता परिक्लिष्टा सभां गता ।
पश्यतां पाण्डुपुत्राणां त्वयि जीवति केशव ॥
lines.iast:
sā'haṃ keśagrahaṃ prāptā parikliṣṭā sabhāṃ gatā |
paśyatāṃ pāṇḍuputrāṇāṃ tvayi jīvati keśava ||
lines.en: And I was dragged by the hair into the hall and tormented, while the sons of Pandu looked on, and while you were alive, Keshava.

lines.deva:
अदासाः पाण्डवाः सन्तु सरथाः सायुधा इति ।
मयोक्ते यत्र निर्मुक्ता वनवासाय केशव ॥
lines.iast:
adāsāḥ pāṇḍavāḥ santu sarathāḥ sāyudhā iti |
mayokte yatra nirmuktā vanavāsāya keśava ||
lines.en: "Let the Pandavas be free, with their chariots and their weapons," I said, and they were released to go to the forest, Keshava.
lines.context: Draupadi recalls the boon Dhritarashtra offered her after the dice game (MBh 5.81.27).

lines.deva:
अयं ते पुण्डरीकाक्ष दुःशासनकरोद्धृतः ।
स्मर्तव्यः सर्वकार्येषु परेषां सन्धिमिच्छताम् ॥
lines.iast:
ayaṃ te puṇḍarīkākṣa duḥśāsanakaroddhṛtaḥ |
smartavyaḥ sarvakāryeṣu pareṣāṃ sandhimicchatām ||
lines.en: Lotus-eyed one, this is the hair Duhshasana's hand pulled. Remember it in everything you do, whenever the other side asks for peace.
lines.context: She holds up her hair in her left hand as she says it (MBh 5.81.33 to 35).

lines.deva:
त्रयोदश हि वर्षाणि प्रतीक्षन्त्या गतानि मे ।
विधाय हृदये मन्युं प्रदीप्तमिव पावकम् ॥
lines.iast:
trayodaśa hi varṣāṇi pratīkṣantyā gatāni me |
vidhāya hṛdaye manyuṃ pradīptamiva pāvakam ||
lines.en: Thirteen years have gone by while I waited, keeping my anger in my heart like a blazing fire.

lines.deva:
तामुवाच महाबाहुः केशवः परिसान्त्वयन् ।
अचिराद्द्रक्ष्यसे कृष्णे रुदतीर्भरतस्त्रियः ॥
lines.iast:
tāmuvāca mahābāhuḥ keśavaḥ parisāntvayan |
acirāddrakṣyase kṛṣṇe rudatīrbharatastriyaḥ ||
lines.en: Keshava comforted her and said: soon, Draupadi, you will see the women of the Bharatas weeping.
lines.note: Krishna addresses her as Kṛṣṇā, her own name; we render it Draupadi in English to avoid confusion with Krishna.

lines.deva:
ब्रूयाः केशव राजानं धर्मात्मानं युधिष्ठिरम् ।
भूयांस्ते हीयते धर्मो मा पुत्रक वृथा कृथाः ॥
lines.iast:
brūyāḥ keśava rājānaṃ dharmātmānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram |
bhūyāṃste hīyate dharmo mā putraka vṛthā kṛthāḥ ||
lines.en: Tell King Yudhishthira, whose heart is set on dharma: much of your dharma is slipping away, my son. Do not let it go to waste.

lines.deva:
माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः ।
मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर ॥
lines.iast:
mā''tmānamavamanyasva mainamalpena bībharaḥ |
manaḥ kṛtvā sukalyāṇaṃ mā bhaistvaṃ pratisaṃhara ||

speaker.en: Vidula to her son, as Kunti tells it
speaker.hi: विदुला, अपने बेटे से (कुंती के मुख से)

lines.en: Do not despise yourself. Do not feed yourself on so little. Set your mind on what is good. Do not be afraid. Pull yourself together.

lines.deva:
मुहूर्तं ज्वलितं श्रेयो न च धूमायितं चिरम् ।
मा ह स्म कस्यचिद्गेहे जनि राज्ञः खरो मृदुः ॥
lines.iast:
muhūrtaṃ jvalitaṃ śreyo na ca dhūmāyitaṃ ciram |
mā ha sma kasyacidgehe jani rājñaḥ kharo mṛduḥ ||

speaker.en: Vidula to her son, as Kunti tells it
speaker.hi: विदुला, अपने बेटे से (कुंती के मुख से)

lines.en: Better to blaze for a moment than to smoulder for years. May no king's house have a son who is only harsh or only soft.
lines.hi: देर तक धुआँ देने से अच्छा है पल भर के लिए धधक उठना।
lines.note: Corpus second half reads "जनी राज्ञः स्वरीमृदुः"; emended to the vulgate "जनि राज्ञः खरो मृदुः". The card uses only the first half.
lines.corpus: मुहूर्तं ज्वलितं श्रेयो न च धूमायितं चिरम् / मा ह स्म कस्यचिद्गेहे जनी राज्ञः स्वरीमृदुः

lines.deva:
अलब्ध्वा यदि वा लब्ध्वा नानुशोचति पण्डितः ।
आनन्तर्यं चारभते न प्राणानां धनायते ॥
lines.iast:
alabdhvā yadi vā labdhvā nānuśocati paṇḍitaḥ |
ānantaryaṃ cārabhate na prāṇānāṃ dhanāyate ||

speaker.en: Vidula to her son, as Kunti tells it
speaker.hi: विदुला, अपने बेटे से (कुंती के मुख से)

lines.en: Whether or not he gets what he wanted, the wise one does not grieve. He takes up the next task at once and does not hoard his life.

lines.deva:
कन्या गर्भं समाधत्त भास्करान्मां जनार्दन ।
आदित्यवचनाच्चैव जातं मां सा व्यसर्जयत् ॥
lines.iast:
kanyā garbhaṃ samādhatta bhāskarānmāṃ janārdana |
ādityavacanāccaiva jātaṃ māṃ sā vyasarjayat ||
lines.en: She conceived me by the Sun while still unmarried, Janardana, and at the Sun's word she let me go once I was born.

lines.deva:
सूतो हि मामधिरथो दृष्ट्वैवाभ्यानयद्गृहान् ।
राधायाश्चैव मां प्रादात्सौहार्दान्मधुसूदन ॥
lines.iast:
sūto hi māmadhiratho dṛṣṭvaivābhyānayadgṛhān |
rādhāyāścaiva māṃ prādātsauhārdānmadhusūdana ||
lines.en: Adhiratha the charioteer saw me and brought me home, and out of love he gave me to Radha, Madhusudana.

lines.deva:
न पृथिव्या सकलया न सुवर्णस्य राशिभिः ।
हर्षाद्भयाद्वा गोविन्द मिथ्या कर्तुं तदुत्सहे ॥
lines.iast:
na pṛthivyā sakalayā na suvarṇasya rāśibhiḥ |
harṣādbhayādvā govinda mithyā kartuṃ tadutsahe ||
lines.en: Not for the whole earth, not for heaps of gold, not out of joy or fear, Govinda, could I make those bonds false.
lines.context: Karna has just named the bonds: Radha who nursed him, Adhiratha who raised him, and the wives, sons and grandsons of his own life (MBh 5.141.5 to 11).

lines.deva:
यदि जानाति मां राजा धर्मात्मा संयतेन्द्रियः ।
कुन्त्याः प्रथमजं पुत्रं न स राज्यं ग्रहीष्यति ॥
lines.iast:
yadi jānāti māṃ rājā dharmātmā saṃyatendriyaḥ |
kuntyāḥ prathamajaṃ putraṃ na sa rājyaṃ grahīṣyati ||
lines.en: If the righteous, self-controlled king learns that I am Kunti's firstborn, he will not take the kingdom.

lines.deva:
कौन्तेयस्त्वं न राधेयो न तवाधिरथः पिता ।
नासि सूतकुले जातः कर्ण तद्विद्धि मे वचः ॥
lines.iast:
kaunteyastvaṃ na rādheyo na tavādhirathaḥ pitā |
nāsi sūtakule jātaḥ karṇa tadviddhi me vacaḥ ||
lines.en: You are Kunti's son, Karna, and Radha did not bear you. Adhiratha is not your father. You were not born among the charioteers. Know this from me.
lines.hi: कर्ण, तुम कुंती के बेटे हो, राधा के नहीं। अधिरथ तुम्हारे पिता नहीं। तुम सूतों के कुल में नहीं जन्मे। मेरी बात जान लो।

lines.deva:
कानीनस्त्वं मया जातः पूर्वजः कुक्षिणा धृतः ।
कुन्तिराजस्य भवने पार्थस्त्वमसि पुत्रक ॥
lines.iast:
kānīnastvaṃ mayā jātaḥ pūrvajaḥ kukṣiṇā dhṛtaḥ |
kuntirājasya bhavane pārthastvamasi putraka ||
lines.en: I bore you before I was married, my firstborn, carried in my womb in King Kuntibhoja's house. You are a son of Pritha, my child.

lines.deva:
अकरोन्मयि यत्पापं भवती सुमहात्ययम् ।
अपाकीर्णोऽस्मि यन्मातस्तद्यशःकीर्तिनाशनम् ॥
lines.iast:
akaronmayi yatpāpaṃ bhavatī sumahātyayam |
apākīrṇo'smi yanmātastadyaśaḥkīrtināśanam ||
lines.en: You did me a great wrong, mother, and it cost me dearly. You cast me away, and that took my name and my standing.

lines.deva:
आनृशंस्यमथो वृत्तं रक्षन्सत्पुरुषोचितम् ।
अतोऽर्थकरमप्येतन्न करोम्यद्य ते वचः ॥
lines.iast:
ānṛśaṃsyamatho vṛttaṃ rakṣansatpuruṣocitam |
ato'rthakaramapyetanna karomyadya te vacaḥ ||
lines.en: Holding to kindness and to the conduct that suits a good man, I will not do what you ask today, though it would profit me.

lines.deva:
न च तेऽयं समारम्भो मयि मोघो भविष्यति ।
वध्यान्विषह्यान्संग्रामे न हनिष्यामि ते सुतान् ॥
lines.iast:
na ca te'yaṃ samārambho mayi mogho bhaviṣyati |
vadhyānviṣahyānsaṃgrāme na haniṣyāmi te sutān ||
lines.en: Yet your coming to me will not be for nothing. In battle I will not kill your sons, though I could.

lines.deva:
न ते जातु नशिष्यन्ति पुत्राः पञ्च यशस्विनि ।
निरर्जुनाः सकर्णा वा सार्जुना वा हते मयि ॥
lines.iast:
na te jātu naśiṣyanti putrāḥ pañca yaśasvini |
nirarjunāḥ sakarṇā vā sārjunā vā hate mayi ||
lines.en: You will never have fewer than five sons, glorious one: five with Karna if Arjuna falls, or five with Arjuna if I am killed.
lines.hi: तुम्हारे पाँच बेटे हमेशा रहेंगे: अर्जुन गिरे तो कर्ण के साथ, मैं मारा जाऊँ तो अर्जुन के साथ।

lines.deva:
एवं वै भाव्यमेतेन क्षयं यास्यन्ति कौरवाः ।
यथा त्वं भाषसे कर्ण दैवं तु बलवत्तरम् ॥
lines.iast:
evaṃ vai bhāvyametena kṣayaṃ yāsyanti kauravāḥ |
yathā tvaṃ bhāṣase karṇa daivaṃ tu balavattaram ||
lines.en: So it must be. The Kauravas will go to ruin, as you say, Karna. Fate is stronger.

lines.deva:
त्वया चतुर्णां भ्रातॄणामभयं शत्रुकर्शन ।
दत्तं तत्प्रतिजानीहि सङ्गरप्रतिमोचनम् ॥
lines.iast:
tvayā caturṇāṃ bhrātṝṇāmabhayaṃ śatrukarśana |
dattaṃ tatpratijānīhi saṅgarapratimocanam ||
lines.en: You have given four of your brothers your word of safety, tamer of foes. Hold to that promise until the battle releases you from it.

lines.deva:
प्रतिज्ञां दुष्करां कृत्वा पितुरर्थे कुलस्य च ।
अराजा चोर्ध्वरेताश्च यथा सुविदितं तव ।
प्रतीतो निवसाम्येष प्रतिज्ञामनुपालयन् ॥
lines.iast:
pratijñāṃ duṣkarāṃ kṛtvā piturarthe kulasya ca |
arājā cordhvaretāśca yathā suviditaṃ tava |
pratīto nivasāmyeṣa pratijñāmanupālayan ||
lines.en: I made a hard vow for my father's sake and for the family's: no throne and no children, as you well know. Keeping that vow, I live content.
lines.context: Krishna reports to the Pandavas what Bhishma said to Duryodhana in the Kuru assembly.

lines.deva:
ततोऽहं प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा मातरं संप्रसादयम् ।
नाम्ब शन्तनुना जातः कौरवं वंशमुद्वहन् ॥
प्रतिज्ञां वितथां कुर्यामिति राजन्पुनः पुनः ।
विशेषतस्त्वदर्थं च प्रतिज्ञां कृतवानहम् ॥
lines.iast:
tato'haṃ prāñjalirbhūtvā mātaraṃ saṃprasādayam |
nāmba śantanunā jātaḥ kauravaṃ vaṃśamudvahan ||
pratijñāṃ vitathāṃ kuryāmiti rājanpunaḥ punaḥ |
viśeṣatastvadarthaṃ ca pratijñāṃ kṛtavānaham ||
lines.en: Then I joined my palms and pleaded with my mother. "Mother, I am Shantanu's son and I carry the Kuru line. I will not make my vow false," I said again and again. "I made that vow for you above all."
lines.context: With the kingdom without a king and the people starving, the citizens and Satyavati beg Bhishma to rule (MBh 5.147.25 to 31).

lines.deva:
लोकस्तं वेद यदहं पितुः प्रियचिकीर्षया ।
प्राप्तं राज्यं परित्यज्य ब्रह्मचर्यव्रते स्थितः ॥
lines.iast:
lokastaṃ veda yadahaṃ pituḥ priyacikīrṣayā |
prāptaṃ rājyaṃ parityajya brahmacaryavrate sthitaḥ ||
lines.en: The world knows that, to please my father, I gave up the kingdom that was mine and held to the vow of celibacy.

lines.deva:
न जातु कामः कामानामुपभोगेन शाम्यति ।
हविषा कृष्णवर्त्मेव भूय एवाभिवर्धते ॥
lines.iast:
na jātu kāmaḥ kāmānāmupabhogena śāmyati |
haviṣā kṛṣṇavartmeva bhūya evābhivardhate ||

speaker.en: Panchashikha to King Janaka, as Bhishma tells it
speaker.hi: पंचशिख, राजा जनक से (भीष्म के मुख से)

lines.en: Desire is never quieted by enjoying what it wants. Like a fire fed with ghee, it only grows.
lines.note: Corpus reads कामामाम् and अभिर्वधते; emended. The line is better known as King Yayati's in the Adi Parva; here it sits in a southern-recension passage of Panchashikha's teaching to Janaka. Speaker attribution needs a check against the full chapter.

speaker.en: The swan to the Sadhyas, as Bhishma tells it
speaker.hi: हंस, साध्य देवों से (भीष्म के मुख से)

lines.en: When cursed, I curse no one back. I know self-control to be the door to the deathless. I tell you a hidden truth: there is nothing higher than being human.
lines.hi: शाप मिलने पर भी मैं किसी को शाप नहीं देता। संयम अमरता का दरवाज़ा है। एक गूढ़ बात कहता हूँ: मनुष्य होने से बढ़कर कुछ नहीं।
lines.context: Bhishma, answering Yudhishthira, tells of Prajapati in the form of a golden swan teaching the Sadhya gods (MBh 12.305.2 to 4).

lines.deva:

एष साङ्ग्राहिको धर्मः कामादन्यः प्रवर्तते ॥
lines.iast:
na tatparasya saṃdadhyātpratikūlaṃ yadātmanaḥ |
eṣa sāṅgrāhiko dharmaḥ kāmādanyaḥ pravartate ||
lines.en: Do not do to another what you would find hateful done to yourself. That is dharma in brief. Anything else comes from desire.
lines.hi: जो बात तुम्हें अपने लिए बुरी लगे, वह दूसरों के साथ मत करो। यही धर्म का सार है, बाकी सब कामना से चलता है।
lines.context: Brihaspati, teacher of the gods, answers Yudhishthira and then leaves for heaven (MBh 13.175.11).

lines.deva:
यत्तु तद्भवता प्रोक्तं पुरा केशव सौहृदात् ।
तत्सर्वं पुरुषव्याघ्र नष्टं मे व्यग्रचेतसः ॥
lines.iast:
yattu tadbhavatā proktaṃ purā keśava sauhṛdāt |
tatsarvaṃ puruṣavyāghra naṣṭaṃ me vyagracetasaḥ ||
lines.en: What you told me then, Keshava, out of friendship, has all slipped away from me, tiger among men, because my mind was scattered.
lines.hi: केशव, आपने तब मित्रता के नाते जो कहा था, मेरे बिखरे मन से वह सब छूट गया।
lines.context: After the war, in the palace at Hastinapura, Arjuna asks Krishna to tell him again what he taught on the battlefield.

lines.deva:
स हि धर्मः सुपर्याप्तो ब्रह्मणः पदवेदने ।
न शक्यं तन्मया भूयस्तथा वक्तुमशेषतः ॥
lines.iast:
sa hi dharmaḥ suparyāpto brahmaṇaḥ padavedane |
na śakyaṃ tanmayā bhūyastathā vaktumaśeṣataḥ ||
lines.en: That teaching was complete for reaching Brahman. I cannot tell it again, in full, the way I did then.
lines.hi: वह धर्म ब्रह्म तक पहुँचने के लिए पूरा था। अब मैं उसे फिर उसी तरह पूरा नहीं कह सकता।
lines.context: Krishna then tells an older story instead, the Anugita, which runs through the next chapters of the Ashvamedhika Parva.
